claim: Nothing on the Production front asks for って, so a learner gives the は form the ledger taught.
evidence: Production front: "Grammar & Function Words / What is an onsen?" with no scene or hint. Ledger teaches これはなんですか ("What is this?"), so おんせんはなんですか is what comes out; the back wants おんせんってなんですか.
fix: Add a scene such as "repeating a word you just heard and do not understand" so the front asks for って.
verdictReason: Checked the faces and the ledger: the Production front is "Grammar & Function Words / What is an onsen?" with no scene or hint, and the ledger has これはなんですか and あれはなんですか, so おんせんはなんですか answers the front. The book's own English keeps quotation marks (What is an "onsen"?) that signal the echoed word; the card dropped them. card-rules-shared requires the hint to name the structure when one English shape maps to two.

claim: The Production English gives no cue for よ, which is the point of the card.
evidence: Production front: "It's a Japanese spa." / "pointing at a photo of an onsen on a smartphone". Back: にほんのスパですよ. The ledger card きれいなところですよ was glossed "It's a pretty place, you know.", so よ has been signalled by "you know" before; here nothing signals it and にほんのスパです fits the front.
fix: Gloss it "It's a Japanese spa, you know." or add a hint that the speaker is telling the listener something new.
verdictReason: Checked: the English is the book's own ("It's a Japanese spa."), the scene says nothing about telling the listener something new, and にほんのスパです satisfies the front. The deck's two earlier よ sentences (chapter-10 きれいなところですよ, chapter-10-extras おもしろいところですよ) both cue it with ", you know", so the precedent exists and this card breaks it. Fixer: a hint keeps the book's English intact; changing the gloss is the alternative.

claim: The hint says ちかく cannot take です, which clashes with the "X は [place] です" pattern the deck has taught.
evidence: Hint on both faces: "the noun for ‘the area near’, so it is followed by に (ni) and あります (arimasu), not です (desu)". The same hint is on ryokan-chikaku-nani-arimasuka, fib-daigaku-no-chikaku-ni-ginkou-ya-yuubinkyoku-ga-arimasu, p12-eki-no-chikaku-ni-yuubinkyoku-mo-arimasu and v12-sofaa-no-chikaku-ni-terebi-ga-arimasu. Ledger: インフォメーションは１かいです, おてあらいはあちらです, so ゆうびんきょくはえきのちかくです looks just as valid.
fix: Drop "not です (desu)" and say only that a "there is" sentence uses ちかくに あります, on all five cards.
verdictReason: True for chikaku-near, whose hint field ends "not です (desu)": えきのちかくです is ordinary Japanese and the book nowhere forbids it. Scope correction: the four sentence cards named in the evidence do NOT carry this hint; theirs reads 'a "there is" sentence ... so it takes にあります', which is the structure-naming hint card-rules-shared requires and says nothing about です. Fix only chikaku-near.

claim: The name Raja is written in hiragana, against every earlier card.
evidence: Learner: Front: "らじゃさんのうちはインドのどこですか". Ledger: "ラジャさんはいしゃです", "はじめまして。とうきょうだいがくのラジャです…", "ラジャさんはいつにほんにきましたか". Reader: Book, SPEAKING PRACTICE 1: "ラジャさんの うちは インドの どこですか。" Card target: "らじゃさんのうちはインドのどこですか". Earlier cards: ラジャさんはいしゃです, ラジャさんのおくにはどちらですか, and nine more, all ラジャ.
fix: Change らじゃさん to ラジャさん in the target (and its audio text if it carries the spelling).
verdictReason: Checked: らじゃ occurs in exactly one cards.json in the collection (chapter-12, this card); ラジャ occurs 24 times across the collection and the book's SPEAKING PRACTICE 1 prints ラジャさんの うちは インドの どこですか. The pronunciation is already "Raja-san" and there is no ttsText, so only the target needs changing (the audio clip regenerates from it; same sound). Preflight does not report it. Learner and Reader found the same bug from opposite sides; merged.

claim: The note describes the substitution the wrong way round.
evidence: Note: "Same frame as なにもありません (nani mo arimasen, ‘there is nothing’), with なに (nani) in place of だれ (dare)." This card is だれもいません, so it is だれ in place of なに, and the verb also changes to いません.
fix: Say "with だれ (dare) in place of なに (nani), and いません (imasen) because it is about people".
verdictReason: Note reads "Same frame as なにもありません ..., with なに (nani) in place of だれ (dare)". The natural reading of "same as B, with X in place of Y" is that this card is B with Y replaced by X, which is backwards for だれもいません; the verb also changes (いません), which the note omits. Wording fix only.

claim: A "plain form" hint sits on a noun, and the learner was never taught what a plain form is.
evidence: Production front: "Food / Soba shop / plain form". Recognition back: "Answer: Soba shop / plain form". Nothing in the ledger defines plain form, and そばや has no other form in this deck.
verdictReason: The hint field is literally "plain form" on a noun card. No other card in the collection uses it as a hint (the phrase appears elsewhere only inside notes about verbs in chapters 11, 24 and 25), そばや has no other form in the deck, and the ledger never defines the term. Stray hint; remove.

evidence: Production front: "There are a big lake, waterfall, and other things." / "answering what is near the Japanese inn".
fix: Use "There are a big lake, a waterfall, and other things."
verdictReason: The book gives no English for this line (EXERCISES VI example), so the gloss is the deck's own. "There are a big lake, waterfall, and other things" is not idiomatic English; the sibling nikko-otera-jinja-arimasu shows the clean shape ("temples, shrines, and other sights").

claim: The romaji spells long vowels with doubled letters where the deck uses macrons, and runs the word together unlike its own word card.
evidence: Learner: Back: "Says: kashuunattsu ga yuumei desu". Word card cashew-nuts: "Says: kashū nattsu"; the deck writes long vowels as ō/ū (e.g. "yūbinkyoku", "chūshajō"). Reader: Card pronunciation: "kashuunattsu ga yuumei desu". Same unit, cashew-nuts: "kashū nattsu"; deck elsewhere: "yūmei".
fix: Change to "kashū nattsu ga yūmei desu".
verdictReason: Checked the pronunciation field: "kashuunattsu ga yuumei desu". card-authoring-rules.md (romaji style) mandates macrons and names yūmei explicitly; "yūmei" appears 7 times elsewhere in the collection and the word card cashew-nuts says "kashū nattsu". Not already reported: preflight's long-vowel-macron rule fires only on "ou" (it flagged kyoukai in fib-goa-donna-tokoro-answer and missed this card). Both roles found it; merged.

claim: The romaji uses "uu" where the deck uses a macron.
evidence: Learner: Back: "Says: nani ga yuumei desu ka". Elsewhere in this unit: "yūbinkyoku", "chūshajō", "kyōkai". Reader: Card pronunciation: "nani ga yuumei desu ka". Deck elsewhere: chapter-10 "yūmei", "fujisan wa yūmei desu".
fix: Change to "nani ga yūmei desu ka".
verdictReason: Checked: pronunciation is "nani ga yuumei desu ka"; the style rule mandates "yūmei" and the collection uses it everywhere else. Preflight's long-vowel-macron rule only catches "ou", so this is not already reported. Both roles found it; merged.

claim: Nothing on the Production front asks for って, so a learner gives the は form the ledger taught.
evidence: Production front: "Travel & Tourism / What is a theme park?" with no scene, hint or note. Ledger: これはなんですか; back wants テーマパークってなんですか.
fix: Add a scene such as "asking about a word someone just used" and a short note on って.
verdictReason: Same defect as onsen-tte-nandesuka: Production front "Travel & Tourism / What is a theme park?" has no scene, hint or note, and this card has no note at all, so nothing on either face explains って. テーマパークはなんですか fits the front from the ledger's これはなんですか.

claim: The romaji uses doubled vowels where the deck uses macrons, unlike its own word card.
evidence: Learner: Back: "Says: teemapaaku tte nan desu ka". Word card teema-paaku: "Says: tēma pāku"; ex12-teemapaaku-ya-onsen-ga-arimasu: "tēmapāku". Reader: Card pronunciation: "teemapaaku tte nan desu ka". chapter-12/teema-paaku: "tēma pāku"; extras ex12-teemapaaku-ya-onsen-ga-arimasu: "tēmapāku".
fix: Change to "tēma pāku tte nan desu ka".
verdictReason: Checked: pronunciation is "teemapaaku tte nan desu ka"; the word card teema-paaku says "tēma pāku" and ex12-teemapaaku-ya-onsen-ga-arimasu says "tēmapāku". Doubled ee/aa is outside what preflight's long-vowel-macron rule catches, so not already reported. Both roles found it; merged.

claim: Nothing on the Production front asks for って, so a learner gives the は form the ledger taught.
evidence: Production front: "Food / What is tempura?" with no scene or hint. Ledger: これはなんですか, あれはなんですか; back wants てんぷらってなんですか.
fix: Add a scene such as "repeating a word you just heard and do not understand".
verdictReason: Same defect as onsen-tte-nandesuka: Production front "Food / What is tempura?" with no scene or hint; the note on the back explains って but nothing on the front asks for it, so てんぷらはなんですか answers the front from the ledger's これはなんですか.

claim: The note talks about a missing の that no learner would have put there, and it confuses more than it helps.
evidence: Note: "かいぎしつ (kaigishitsu) takes に (ni) directly with no の (no) in front, because it is already a place noun rather than a position word."
fix: Replace with a note that adds something, or drop it.
verdictReason: The note is accurate and verifiable from this chapter: GRAMMAR 2 gives noun1 の noun2(position) for position words, and the の it means is the one in つくえのしたに / となりのへやに that the unit drills alongside this card. A place noun taking に directly is a real contrast for a learner building sentences from the same frame. Whether it helps is a judgement; it is not unverifiable and no rule forbids it.

claim: The note calls brown "the other both-ways colour" without saying which colour is the first.
evidence: Note: "ちゃいろ (chairo) is the other both-ways colour, so ちゃいろのつくえ (chairo no tsukue) is equally fine." The ledger has both きいろい and きいろの, but the note does not name it.
fix: Name the pair: "Like きいろ (kiiro), ちゃいろ works both ways: ちゃいろい or ちゃいろの".
verdictReason: The fact is taught (chapter-5-extras notes on きいろい and ちゃいろい both name the pair), but this note's "the other both-ways colour" has no referent on the card, and the learner meets it months later in isolation. Naming きいろ is a three-word fix.

claim: The note gives the wrong lesson for いきました.
evidence: Note: "its past is built exactly like たべました (tabemashita) and いきました (ikimashita) in Lesson 8." Ledger: いきました is taught in Lesson 6 (スミスさんはせんしゅうおおさかにいきました).
verdictReason: Ledger confirms: いきました is first carded in Lesson 6 (chapter-6: いきました | Went, plus four sentences), while たべました first appears in Lesson 8 (chapter-8). The note attributes both to Lesson 8.

claim: The よこ note glosses its example as "next to", which is the English the となり card uses as its Production front.
evidence: side note: "いすの よこ (isu no yoko) = 'next to the chair'". chapter-12/tonari-next-to Production front: "Directions / Next to", answer となり.
fix: Gloss the example "beside the chair" and keep "next to" for となり.
verdictReason: The facts hold: the side note glosses いすの よこ as 'next to the chair' and 'Next to' is the Production English of tonari-next-to (also 'What is next to the Japanese inn?' on ex12-ryokan-no-tonari-ni-nani-ga-arimasu-ka). The collision is a back-note example gloss, not a front: side's Production front is "Side", so no face is unanswerable. Polish stands; 'beside' keeps 'next to' for となり.

claim: The English drops the book’s sense of the question, which asks what the place is famous for.
evidence: Book, SPEAKING PRACTICE 1: "なにが ゆうめいですか。" / "Nakamura: What is it famous for?" Card English: "What is famous?"
fix: Use the book’s English, "What is it famous for?", or "What is famous there?".
verdictReason: Book SPEAKING PRACTICE 1 prints なにが ゆうめいですか with the English "What is it famous for?". The card is flagged fillInBlank/aiSuggested (rendered 'authored for the deck') but the sentence is verbatim in the book, so the book's English is available and the word-for-word "What is famous?" loses the sense.

claim: The note calls って a casual contraction and names とはなんですか as its formal equivalent, which the book does not say and never teaches.
evidence: Book, NOTES 1: "〜って なんですか is the way part of something one has heard may be repeated in order to ask what it means." Card note: "って (tte) is a casual contraction ... It stands in for は (wa) here; the formal equivalent is とはなんですか (to wa nan desu ka)."
fix: Trim the note to the book’s point: って picks up a word you just heard to ask what it means.
verdictReason: Book NOTES 1 says only that 〜って なんですか repeats part of something heard to ask what it means; it does not call って casual, and とは appears nowhere in the book or in any card of the collection (grep). The note asserts a register and a formal equivalent the learner cannot check.

claim: The note states Kamakura was Japan’s capital in the 12th and 13th centuries, which the book does not say and which is loose (it was the shogunate’s seat until 1333; Kyoto remained the imperial capital).
evidence: Book vocabulary: "かまくら Kamakura (historic area south of Tokyo)". Card note: "かまくら (kamakura) was Japan’s capital in the 12th and 13th centuries and is an easy day trip from Tokyo."
fix: Say it was the seat of the shogun’s government from the late 12th century, or keep only the book’s "historic area south of Tokyo" and the day-trip remark.
verdictReason: Book vocabulary glosses only "Kamakura (historic area south of Tokyo)" and the chapter says nothing more. Kamakura was the seat of the Kamakura shogunate (1185 to 1333) while the imperial capital stayed in Kyoto, so "Japan's capital in the 12th and 13th centuries" is loose and unsupported by the book.
